boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations in downtown Lowell’s historic canal district, each paired with one documented reason to pause along a nearby corridor.

cards.entity_name: Lowell National Historical Park Visitor Center
cards.title: Start with the city’s industrial-story exhibits
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — 246 Market Street
cards.notes: Begin on Market Street to use the orientation exhibits, then ask a ranger about walking or canal tours before choosing your next downtown stop.
cards.short_summary: A staffed orientation point with exhibits and tour information.
cards.evidence_claim: The Visitor Center has exhibits on Lowell’s industrial and community history and is used to join walking and canal tours.
cards.source_title: Visitor Center — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: At 246 Market Street; consult the park’s current operating-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Read the former mill complex in place
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — 246 Market Street
cards.notes: Stand in the Market Mills courtyard and compare the surviving mill buildings with the canal-side setting before continuing along Market Street.
cards.short_summary: A former textile complex now containing the park visitor center.
cards.evidence_claim: Market Mills began as the Lowell Manufacturing Company complex, and its Brussels Weave Mill is the oldest surviving building in that complex.
cards.source_title: Lowell Waterways Redevelopment Rove — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: The walking route begins at Market Mills, 246 Market Street.

cards.title: Pick up the Waterpower Walk
cards.subtitle: Market Street and Shattuck Street corridor
cards.notes: Use Mack Plaza as the handoff from Market Street to the Waterpower Walk, then follow the route to notice how the canals shaped downtown.
cards.short_summary: A documented starting point for the park’s Waterpower Walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The park directs visitors to pick up the Waterpower Walk at Mack Plaza, at the corner of Shattuck and Market streets.
cards.source_title: Redevelopment Rove Part 2 — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: At the corner of Shattuck and Market streets, across from the Visitor Center.

cards.title: Compare two exhibits about Lowellians
cards.subtitle: French Street corridor — 40 French Street
cards.notes: Enter from French Street and move through the boarding-house and One City, Many Cultures exhibits to connect industrial and community histories.
cards.short_summary: A free exhibit center with two perspectives on Lowell’s residents.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mogan Cultural Center contains the Into an 1840s Boarding House and One City, Many Cultures exhibits, and admission is free.
cards.source_title: Places To Go — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: At 40 French Street; the park lists free admission and recommends checking operating hours.

cards.title: Use the park as a downtown festival landmark
cards.subtitle: French Street corridor — beside 40 French Street
cards.notes: Pause at the green beside the Mogan Cultural Center, then check the park calendar if you want to pair the stop with a scheduled cultural event.
cards.short_summary: A named public park and recurring downtown performance setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Boarding House Park is open daily, and the Lowell Folk Festival uses it as one of its downtown performance locations.
cards.source_title: Operating Hours & Seasons — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Listed at 40 French Street and open daily; event programming varies.

cards.title: See a working loom room
cards.subtitle: John Street corridor — 115 John Street
cards.notes: Visit during museum hours for the recreated weave room, where operating power looms make the industrial setting tangible rather than abstract.
cards.short_summary: A mill museum with a recreated working 1920s-era weave room.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum includes a recreated 1920s-era weave room with operating power looms, artifacts, interactive exhibits, and videos.
cards.source_title: Boott Cotton Mills Museum — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: At 115 John Street; museum admission is ticketed and operating hours are seasonal.

cards.title: Trace waterpower to a still-operating turbine
cards.subtitle: Suffolk Street corridor — 660 Suffolk Street
cards.notes: Book or join the guided option when available, then look for how the Northern Canal sits beside the turbine exhibit’s historic machinery.
cards.short_summary: A guided-tour site centered on a nineteenth-century water turbine.
cards.evidence_claim: The exhibit’s still-operating turbine dates to 1853 and demonstrates how nineteenth-century Lowell mills generated power.
cards.source_title: Places To Go — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: At 660 Suffolk Street alongside the Northern Canal; accessible by guided tour only.

cards.title: Read Kerouac excerpts in the memorial plaza
cards.subtitle: Bridge Street corridor — Kerouac Park
cards.notes: Walk the commemorative path in Kerouac Park and read the installed excerpts, using the circles and cross as part of the artist’s intended design.
cards.short_summary: A memorial plaza dedicated to Lowell-born writer Jack Kerouac.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jack Kerouac Commemorative in Kerouac Park contains excerpts from Kerouac’s writing and was dedicated in 1988.
cards.source_title: Jack Kerouac — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Located in Kerouac Park on Bridge Street.

cards.title: Spot the former medicine laboratory building
cards.subtitle: Market Street corridor — entry/gallery on Middle Street
cards.notes: View the restored Ayer building from Market Street, then use the park’s account to identify its earlier laboratory role and later artist-loft conversion.
cards.short_summary: A restored former laboratory building with a documented adaptive reuse.
cards.evidence_claim: The J. C. Ayer Company used the building for manufacturing laboratories until 1917; it reopened as artist work-and-live lofts in 2000.
cards.source_title: Redevelopment Rove Part 2 — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: On Market Street; the source notes first-floor gallery entry on Middle Street.

cards.title: Find the painted patent-medicine sign
cards.subtitle: Palmer Street corridor — near Market Street
cards.notes: Walk one block down Palmer Street from Market Street and look up at the preserved Father John’s lettering and Carleton & Hovey company plaque.
cards.short_summary: A former medicine-company building identifiable by its surviving signage.
cards.evidence_claim: The Carleton & Hovey Company moved its headquarters and main laboratory to this building in 1920, and its Father John’s signage remains visible.
cards.source_title: Redevelopment Rove Part 2 — Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: On Palmer Street, about one block from Market Street; view from the public street.
